concerns: D20 (decisions.md): registering PortalRolePermissionBackend (T012) — required verbatim by T011's acceptance criteria and by T017's own requirement that a Data Curator reach another team's private dataset by role alone — makes four pre-existing tests fail, none of which this story authored or may modify: tests/test_core/test_dataset/test_plugins.py::TestUpdatePageDoesNotDiscloseAPrivateDataset::test_a_model_level_holder_with_no_record_level_grant_is_refused, tests/test_core/test_dataset/test_plugins.py::TestEachOfTheFourPagesGuardsAPrivateDatasetsVisibility::test_every_page_refuses_a_model_level_holder_with_no_grant_on_this_record, tests/test_core/test_project/test_plugins.py::TestTheOverviewGuardsAPrivateProjectsVisibility::test_every_page_refuses_a_model_level_holder_with_no_grant_on_this_record, and tests/test_core/test_project/test_plugins.py::TestUpdatePageOverHTTP::test_a_user_holding_only_model_level_change_permission_is_refused. These four pin a defect an earlier feature (its own, differently-numbered D14) deliberately fixed: a user holding only a model-level change permission, with no per-record grant, used to be refused on a private Project/Dataset's Update/Delete/Descriptions pages ('a page that relies on inheriting a visibility rule is not guarded at all', per that test's own docstring). PortalRolePermissionBackend reopens exactly that, by design, because this story's own acceptance requires it. Confirmed mechanical: reverting only the AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS entry (with fairdm/permissions.py otherwise unchanged) makes all four pass again. Not touched, per this story's own prohibition on editing a test it did not author when the fix is not a bug in the diff but an earlier assumption ceasing to hold on purpose — that is Sam's call to ratify, not mine. Full analysis, evidence and the revisit condition are in decisions.md D20. The full-suite final verify below runs 2761 passed, 8 skipped, 4 failed — these four and no others.

fairdm/contrib/import_export/views.py's two check() methods (DataImportView.check, DatasetPublishConfirm.check) call user.has_perm("import_data", instance) and user.has_perm("can_publish", instance) without the required "dataset." app-label prefix, so neither call can ever resolve True through any backend — a distinct, pre-existing defect from the one this story addresses. Not named in T018 (which named only the is_data_admin removal) and not exercised by any test because the module fails to import on its own for the unrelated reason above. Left alone.
